title: Redirected, Not Removed: Task-Dependent Stereotyping Reveals the Limits of LLM Alignments

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluated using a 7-task framework spanning explicit probes (e.g., decision making) to implicit probes (e.g., fill-in-the-blank, implicit association tests) using structured templates to test themes like domestic roles, professional roles, autonomy, and personality traits.
Evaluated using a 7-task framework spanning explicit to implicit probes to test themes such as social norms, occupational stereotypes, education, and appearance across different caste identities.
Evaluated using a 7-task framework spanning explicit to implicit probes to test stereotypical associations regarding criminality, culture, identity, education, and personality.
Evaluated using a 7-task framework spanning explicit to implicit probes to test themes such as criminalization, beliefs, occupational stereotypes, personality, and media representation.
Evaluated using a 7-task framework spanning explicit to implicit probes to test biases related to lifestyle, language, criminality, and social etiquette across different class backgrounds.

Evaluated using a 7-task framework spanning explicit to implicit probes to test biases surrounding mental health, chronic illness, and physical disability, focusing on stigma, stereotypical traits, and healthcare access.
Evaluated using a 7-task framework spanning explicit to implicit probes to test linguistic stereotypes, specifically associating different global English accents with intelligence or backwardness.
Evaluated using a 7-task framework spanning explicit to implicit probes to test partisan and ideological associations regarding nationalism, leader traits, and skewed media narratives.

Evaluated using a 7-task framework spanning explicit to implicit probes to test associations regarding subjective traits like intelligence, work ethic, and morality across high-income and low-income nations.
